record.context_brief: Abelianity of Galois groups unramified outside S
record.original_question: Let K be a number field contained in C, and let S be a finite set of places of Q, possibly including archimedean places. Let G_{K,S} be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic subfield of C that is unramified outside S. Is there any example in which G_{Q,S} is abelian even though S contains at least one finite prime?

evidence.quote: Let K be a number field contained in C and S a finite set of places of Q (possibly including archimedean places). Let G_{K,S} be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic subfield of C which is unramified outside of S.
Problem: Can one find instances where G_{Q,S} is abelian when S contains at least one finite prime?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Fix an algebraic closure of the rationals inside the complex numbers. For a finite set S of places of Q (allowed to include the archimedean place), let Q_S denote the maximal algebraic subfield of C that is unramified outside S, and let G_{Q,S} = Gal(Q_S/Q) be its absolute Galois group over Q. Determine whether there exists any finite set S of places of Q that contains at least one finite (non-archimedean) prime such that G_{Q,S} is an abelian group. Equivalently, decide whether there is a finite prime p (possibly together with the archimedean place and/or other finite primes) such that every finite Galois extension of Q unramified outside S has abelian Galois group.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question. It is widely expected that whenever S contains a finite prime there exist nonabelian extensions of Q unramified outside S (e.g., extensions such as Q(2^{1/4}, i) for S = {2, ∞}), but a definitive citation establishing this in full generality for all such S was not located. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On Galois groups of unramified pro-p extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Galois groups of maximal pro-p extensions unramified outside S and known abelian/nonabelian behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the structure of G_{Q,S} continues; no general theorem identifying all S making G_{Q,S} abelian was located.

status_evidence.title: Number fields unramified away from 2 (J. W. Jones)
status_evidence.snippet: Catalogues number fields unramified outside 2, including nonabelian examples.
status_evidence.claim: Nonabelian extensions of Q unramified outside 2 exist, suggesting G_{Q,{2,∞}} is nonabelian.
